gen-dafont-joystix-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Widely tracked and arcade-loud, Joystix has stems barely heavier than its arms. Be Vietnam Pro, a plain sans, bends its strokes like steel rod with a high mean line, so the two feel like pixel signage beside clean vinyl lettering.
gen-dafont-joystix-fs-familjen-grotesk: Chunky, spaced-out, pure arcade cabinet. Familjen Grotesk, a sans with tall lowercase and bowls left open on one side, feels livelier and looser beside Joystix's rigid, gently swelling curves.
gen-dafont-joystix-fs-hoover: Hoover reads robust and refined, its e opening generously despite short, compressed ascenders. Joystix is best at loud, widely tracked display letters, while this text serif does its best work in steady, compact running lines.
gen-dafont-joystix-fs-nunito: Loud, spaced-out and unmistakably arcade. Nunito, a sans with big round lowercase bowls and terminals that stop well clear of the stem, can sit at a generous size so its friendliness comes through under Joystix.
gen-dafont-joystix-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Joystix brings widely tracked, arcade-bold letters whose heavy strokes soften gently into light ones. Pilcrow Rounded runs on in a tight, warm sans with tall lowercase and open curves.
gen-dafont-joystix-fs-trench-slab: Wide-tracked arcade letters, stems just heavier than their arms, mark Joystix at once. Trench Slab, a classic serif with caps and lowercase sitting close in height, gives that playfulness a dignified, refined partner.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Joystix earns its keep big and short, where its bold, widely tracked arcade letters can stand alone. Noto Sans Deseret, a plain sans with open apertures and squat ascenders, stays approachable and clean beneath it.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-noto-sans-newa: Noto Sans Newa is a modern sans-serif with a clearly open e and tall, generous bowls. And its easy openness is the pair's strongest quality, set against Joystix's gentle modulation and bold arcade stance.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-sono: Sono spaces its tall lowercase widely, with each a left slightly ajar, so it feels approachable and professional. Its openness is the strongest thing here against Joystix.
gen-dafont-junegull-bitter: Friendly and retro, Junegull pinches its curves nearly shut and keeps its o ring at constant thickness. Bitter, a slab-serif with a big open lowercase eye and see-through s, would read in a dependable, grounded way over many lines.
